global_read: global.json (11:20) shows Brent at $92.17 (+1.27% 1d, +18.32% 1mo) -- a fresh multi-week high directly corroborating this checkpoint's escalation trigger -- while WTI sits at $85.25 (+0.40%/+13.94%). Equities/vol remain surprisingly calm for the scale of the geopolitical shock: S&P +0.89%, Dow +0.74%, VIX down again to 17.05 (-8.58% 1d), i.e. global risk appetite has NOT yet repriced this specific escalation (Kuwaiti tanker hit, Houthi blockade threat, 10th day of US-Iran strikes) -- a decoupling this desk treats with caution rather than comfort, since PSX's own transmission channel is the oil-import-bill/PKR/reserves path, not the S&P/VIX tape. PKR/USD 277.48 (+0.36% 1d) and DXY 101.11 (-0.06% 1d) both still calm -- the rupee has not (yet) cracked under this fresh oil leg, but that is precisely the channel to watch into the 07-27 MPC.
drivers: Brent crude topped $92.71/bbl intraday (Yahoo/global.json print $92.17, +1.27-1.87% 1d, a fresh ~6-week high) on a 10th consecutive day of US strikes on Iran, with Tehran reported to have struck US-linked sites in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation; oil desks describe the interim peace deal from last month as 'all but wrecked' (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-21/another-tanker-hit-in-hormuz-as-houthis-add-to-regional-risks)

A Kuwait-flagged tanker (the Kaifan, owned by Kuwait Oil Tanker Co.) was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz northeast of Oman's Limah on 2026-07-21, forcing the crew to abandon ship; UKMTO confirmed the incident (https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/hormuz_sees_another_ship_attack_as_houthis_deepen_risks-21-jul-2026-184171-article/, https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-iran-hits-tanker-in-strait-of-hormuz-as-us-air-strikes-continue/)

Yemen's Houthi movement announced a full maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia on 2026-07-20, declaring vessels servicing Saudi ports will no longer be permitted safe passage through Bab al-Mandab -- Saudi crude tankers are reported reversing course in the Red Sea as a direct result, widening the shipping-risk channel beyond Hormuz alone (https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/houthi-threats-force-saudi-crude-tankers-to-reverse-course-in-red-sea-126072101650_1.html, https://cryptobriefing.com/houthis-saudi-blockade-red-sea-tankers/)

Pakistan has formally requested a $10bn Bilateral Exchange Stabilization Support Facility (up to 5-year maturity) from the US Treasury, per Reuters sourcing, following Finance Minister Aurangzeb's Washington meeting with Treasury Secretary Bessent -- a potential reserves/PKR backstop tied to Pakistan's raised diplomatic profile from Iran-war mediation, but NOT yet approved and neither Pakistan's finance ministry nor US Treasury has confirmed on record; no IMF comment on the request found this run (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619526/pakistan-seeks-10-billion-in-us-backstop-facility-to-boost-reserves-source-says, https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/22/pakistan-requests-10-billion-us-facility-to-support-foreign-exchange-reserves/)

Government has shifted to a DAILY fuel-price-revision mechanism (approved by PM Shehbaz Sharif and the federal cabinet, effective mid-July 2026): OGRA now calculates and publishes ex-depot MS/HSD prices every day off a 7-working-day rolling average of Platts Arab Gulf assessments, without prior PM/cabinet sign-off -- a structural adaptation that will pass this oil spike through to pump prices faster than the old fortnightly cycle, raising near-term inflation-pass-through risk while reducing OMC/refiner margin-lag risk (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618933/govt-shifts-to-daily-pol-pricing-amid-global-headwinds, https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/07/20/pakistan-overhauls-fuel-pricing-how-the-revised-mechanism-will-work)

SBP policy rate remains at 11.5% pending the 2026-07-27 MPC (first FY27 decision); no new decision this run -- still tracking the Topline Securities survey (97% hold expected) verified last cycle. CPI unchanged at 11.1% YoY (June 2026 print); July print not due until ~2026-08-01. IMF EFF/RSF program status unchanged since the 2026-05-08 3rd EFF/2nd RSF review completion -- no fresher IMF statement found this run, including none referencing Pakistan's new ESF request (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/21/sbp-likely-to-keep-interest-rate-unchanged/, https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf)

SBP FX reserves last verified at $17.226bn for the week ended 2026-07-10 (down $1.245bn w/w on external debt repayments); dedicated search this run for a week-ended-07-17 print returned nothing published yet -- reserves trajectory is the last verified read heading into a fresh oil-import-bill leg (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618658/reserves-down-124b-on-debt-repayments)

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, 11:20) reads 63/100 'moderate' composite, but its conflict/escalation (100/100) and energy-shock-via-Brent (90/100) sub-factors are both pinned at or near maximum stress -- directly consistent with today's tanker-strike/blockade escalation. Per desk practice this argues against any regime upgrade even though VIX/equities (global.json) remain calm (state/georisk.json)

Net regime read: this checkpoint's escalation (fresh Brent highs, a Kuwaiti tanker struck, a Houthi blockade of Saudi shipping, a 10th day of US-Iran strikes) intensifies rather than eases the oil-driven domestic channel (import bill, reserves, PKR, inflation) that was already holding the desk at risk-off; the $10bn ESF request is a genuine but unconfirmed/unapproved future mitigant, not a present-tense offset. Regime held at risk-off, not downgraded further only because PKR and the equity/vol tape have not yet cracked
